summary: Sonoma/Lake/Napa tri-county lookout on Mount St. Helena, dedicated 1935, replaced 1950 (809R plan); staffing ended 1992 and it was later removed. Summit now has communications towers.

facts.design: 1935 lookout on a 30-foot enclosed tower, similar to a USFS BC-301 cabin plan; 1950 replacement tower conformed closely to the 809R plan
facts.status_note: Removed some time after staffing ended in 1992; the register gives no removal date and no source describes what remains

access.note: On foot only, per a 1991 register note; hikers reach the summit from Robert Louis Stevenson State Park along a fire road

visit.trail_note: No lookout to climb. The Mount St. Helena Trail from Robert Louis Stevenson State Park is 5.3 miles with a 2,100-foot climb, to a summit with several communications towers

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

events.note: Constructed and dedicated in 1935 on a 30-foot enclosed tower (register; newspapers of 1934-35 describe the tri-county station)
Hjalmer Lundell, a former radio operator, named fire lookout in July 1935; a September 1935 report names Henry Lundell
Became a repeater station for the Sonoma County police radio system
An 85-mile-an-hour wind blew an aerial down and damaged the weather station
1935 lookout replaced by a tower that conformed closely to the 809R plan
Register: the lookout ceased to be staffed in 1992
After a statewide review of lookouts, a decision was made to cut funding for Mt. St. Helena

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the lookout's construction and dedication to 1935 and its replacement to 1950. The record's 1950 is the replacement tower's date; the story gives both.

The Napa hiking guide gives 5.3 miles for the Mount St. Helena Trail; Wikipedia gives about 6 miles for the trails from the park. The figures differ by route and source, and the story gives the guide's figure and notes the difference.
Two 1935 newspaper reports name the lookout's operator as Hjalmer Lundell (July) and Henry Lundell (September). Not resolved: the sources do not say whether these are the same man.

sources.title: Robert Louis Stevenson State Park - Mount St. Helena

notes_for_editor: Good newspaper detail (1934-46, via the Forest Lookouts transcriptions, not checked against the original papers). The removal date is unknown: the record says 'After 1992' and the register says 'some time after that', so no removal event is dated. Current condition and public access are from two hiking guides and a 1991 register note; no source describes what remains of the lookout. The Lundell first-name conflict is unresolved. The register's 1946 and 1950 photo credits (Sonoma County Library; rntl.net) were not verified as new finds, so no photos entry was added. Elevation: the register gives 4,340 ft (1,323 m), matching the record's 1322.8 m.
